title: Pressing B picks a Brush that paints freehand strokes onto a paint layer, one undo step per stroke
goal: The first slice of painting: a Brush tool on the tool bar, on B, that paints a freehand stroke in the foreground colour wherever you drag. Strokes land on their own Paint layer so the picture underneath is never changed, the brush stays in your hand for the next stroke, and Command Z takes one stroke off at a time.
notes:
Umbrella: a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal (the user's ask, 2026-10-24). Design: docs/design/brushes.md, read it first; its decisions are settled unless this task's runner finds one cannot work, in which case they say so in the log and in the doc.

Scope: decisions 1, 2, 3, 4 (placement half only) and 5 (live overlay) of the design doc. Marking is one plain round tip with a soft edge, used for every medium for now; the medium slices replace it. The medium enum and its settings list (decision 7) are defined here in PhotonzCore with all seven media and their settings, so later slices fill in looks rather than reshaping the model.

TDD in PhotonzCore: BrushMedium (7 cases, each with its settings list: id, plain name, range, default), BrushSettings (medium + values, clamped to the spec), StrokeSample (point, pressure?, tilt?, ms), BrushStroke (samples, settings, colour hex, seed), PaintContent (strokes), LayerContent.paint, and the dab placement (spacing, size, opacity, deterministic jitter from the seed). PhotonzRender: PaintRasterizer replays strokes into a CGImage at the bake scale, wired into DocumentRenderer like .path (DocumentRenderer.swift ~1337). Every exhaustive switch over LayerContent gets an honest answer for .paint (the compiler lists them; about 25 files switch on .path). SVG export embeds the paint layer as a picture. Tool.brush with shortcut B (Tools.swift ~102 reserves B for brushes).

The brush is the one making tool that does NOT hand back Select after landing (design decision 3): ArrowCaptionEntry.toolAfterLanding must keep .brush.

KEY CLASH, settled by UX-PATTERNS §7 (no card): B is already the Blade on documents with time (EditorView.swift ~1415, EditorCommands.swift ~1281 Edit > Tools Blade row, TimelineKeys.swift ~242). Photoshop's B wins on a picture; the video workspace carries no Brush (PRODUCT-MODEL.md), so the Brush is left off the bar in timed documents and B stays the Blade there. Test it: B on a picture picks the Brush, B on a video still cuts.

CODE MAP (from the planning run, 2026-10-24; line numbers approximate):
- Tools.swift: add case brush; shortcutKey "b"; annotationShape nil; NOT in preservesLayerSelection; doubleClickOnEmptyCanvasZoomsWindow false (ToolTests ~105); createsLayers true; colorControl .toolColor beside the Pen (that is what shows the swatches; paints = colorControl != .hidden).
- AnnotationStyles.swift: the Pen is special-cased (strokeWidthWasChosen, colorHex, strokeWidth, setStrokeWidth, setColorHex, paint, setPaint, usesStrokeWidth); mirror for the brush's armed colour and size.
- ToolBarLayout.swift bar(withFrame:withLens:withPen:withComponent:withHand:): add withBrush (default false) and append .tool(.brush) at the end of drawing. Experiments.swift toolBarLayout passes the flags; FeatureCatalog.swift: a next-brush flag, releases [.next], enabledByDefaultIn [.next] (the feature must be reachable at Next defaults).
- ToolGroupButton.swift barSymbol ("paintbrush.pointed") and barTitle; EditorView.swift ToolbarSlot case brush, its title, menuSymbol, tool, the ungrouped-bar filter, slotButtonBody toolButton(.brush, ...), styleButtonTip. Menu row comes for free from ToolMenu.tools(layout).
- Tests: ToolTests flaggedTools and onlyPaintingToolsCarryColour painting set; ArrowCaptionEntryTests creating set (and the brush stays in hand: ArrowCaptionEntry.toolAfterLanding must return .brush for .brush).
- Canvas: CanvasPointerDrags.swift mouseDown (Pen dispatch ~267), mouseDragged (~859), mouseUp (~1314); mirror CanvasPen.swift (penMouseDown/Dragged/Up, setUpPenChrome, refreshPenChrome) with a CanvasBrush.swift whose live overlay is a CALayer showing a bitmap of the stroke's bounds painted by the same marking code. CanvasView.swift tool state and callbacks (onPathCommit pattern); EditorCanvasSurface.swift wiring (onPathCommit: { editorState.addPath($0) }).
- Commit: mirror EditorState+Pen.swift addPath: one perform (EditorState.perform -> History.perform). New layer via addDrawnLayer when no paint layer is picked; otherwise append the stroke to the picked paint layer in one perform. Do NOT call finishCreating with Select.
- Also: CanvasPointerCue.swift cursor list, CanvasDrawLanding.swift toolStartsAShape, EditorState.setTool.
- Pressure/tilt: nothing reads them yet; record event.pressure in the handlers now (nil for a mouse) so the pressure slice only adds the dynamics.
- Tool options capsule: ToolSettingsBar.swift (enum ToolSetting, settings(for:)) and ToolSettingsCapsule.swift; leave the capsule to the settings slice, but a Size field there is welcome if cheap.
acceptance: Brush (B) sits on the Next tool bar at default settings, with its icon, tooltip and a Tools menu row; B picks it and the colour swatches show while it is in hand
Dragging on a picture paints a smooth stroke in the foreground colour that follows the pointer while you drag, and what lands when you let go looks the same as what you saw while dragging
The first stroke makes a layer called Paint above the picked layer and picks it; the next strokes go onto that same layer; the picture underneath is unchanged
Each stroke is one undo step and redo puts it back; the brush stays in hand after a stroke; a saved and reopened document shows the same strokes
A walk with no flags paints two strokes by pointer drag, photographs them, undoes one and photographs again
